chapters.title_en: The Introduction — On the Praise of God, the Occasion of the Work, and the Enumeration of its Ten Chapters
chapters.arabic_text:
### | المقدمة

[1] الحمد لله الحي القيوم الذي لا يستولي على كنه قيامه وصف واصف الجليل
الذي لا يحيط بصفة جلاله معرفة عارف العزيز الذي لا عزيز إلا وهو بقدم
الصغار على عتبة عزه عاكف الماجد الذي لا ملك إلا وهو حول سرادق مجده طائف
الجبار الذي لا سلطان إلا وهو لنفحات عفوه راج وسطوات سخطه خائف المتكبر
الذي لا ولي إلا وقلبه على محبته وقف وقالبه لخدمته واقف الرحيم الذي لا شئ
إلا وهو ممتط متن الخطر في هول المواقف لولا ترصده لرحمته بوعده السابق
السالف المنعم الذي إن يردك بخير فليس لفضله راد ولا صارف المنتقم الذي ان
يمسسك بضر فما له سواه كاشف جل جلاله وتقدست اسماؤه فلا يغره موالف ولا
يضره مخالف وعز سلطانه فلا يكيده مراوغ ولا يناوئه مكاشف خلق الخلق أحزابا
وأحسابا ورتبهم في زخارف الدنيا أرذالا وأشرافا وقربهم في حقائق الدين
ارتباطا وانحرافا وجهلة وعرافا وفرقهم في قواعد العقائد فرقا وأصنافا
يتطابقون إئتلافا ويتقاطعون اختلافا فافترقوا في المعتقدات جحودا واعترافا
وتعسفا وانصافا واعتدالا وإسرافا كما تباينوا أصلا وأوصافا هذا غني يتضاعف
كل يوم ما له أضعافا وهو يأخذ جزافا وينفق جزافا وهذا ضعيف يعول ذرية ضعافا
يعوزه قوت يوم حتى سأل الناس إلحافا وهذا مقبول في القلوب لا يلقي في حاجته
إلا إجابة وإسعافا وهذا مبغض للخلق تهتضم حقوقه ضيما وإجحافا وهذا تقي موفق
يزداد كل يوم في ورعه وتقواه إسرافا وإشراقا وهذا مخذول يزداد على مر
الأيام
في غيه وفساده تماديا واعتسافا ذلكم تقدير ربكم القادر الحكيم الذي لا
يستطيع سلطان عن قهره انحرافا القاهر العليم الذي لا يملك احد لحكمه خلافا
رغما لأنف الكفرة الباطنية الذين انكروا أن يجعل الله بين أهل الحق اختلافا
ولم يعلموا ان الاختلاف بين الأمة يتبعه الرحمة كما تتبع العبرة اختلافهم
مراتب وأوصافا
وشكرا لله الذي وفقنا للإعتراف بدينه إعلانا وإسرارا وسددنا للإنقياد
لحكمه إظهارا وإضمارا ولم يجعلنا من ضلال الباطنيه الذين يظهرون باللسان
إقرارا ويضمرون في الجنان  تماديا وإصرارا ويحملون من الذنوب اوقارا ويعلنون
في الدين تقوى ووقارا ويحتقبون من المظالم أوزارا لانهم لا يرجون لله وقارا
ولو خاطبهم دعاة الحق ليلا ونهارا لم يزدهم دعاؤهم إلا فرارا فإذا أطل
عليهم سيف أهل الحق آثروا الحق إيثارا وإذا انقشع عنهم ظله أصروا واستكبروا
استكبارا فنسأل الله أن لا يدع على وجه الأرض منهم ديارا ونصلي على رسوله
المصطفى وعلى آله وخلفائه الراشدين من بعده صلوات بعدد قطر السحاب تهمى
مدرارا وتزداد على ممر الأيام استمرارا وتتجدد على توالي الأعوام تلاحقا
وتكرارا
أما بعد فإني لم أزل مدة المقام بمدينة السلام متشوفا إلى أن أخدم
المواقف المقدسة النبوية الامامية المستظهرية ضاعف الله جلالها ومد على
طبقات
الخلق ظلالها بتصنيف كتاب في علم الدين أقضى به شكر النعمة وأقيم به رسم
الخدمة واجتني بما اتعاطاه من الكلفة ثمار القبول والزلفة لكني جنحت الى
التواني لتحري في تعيين العلم الذي اقصده بالتصنيف وتخصيص الفن الذي يقع
موقع الرضا من الرأي النبوي الشريف فكانت هذه الحيرة تغبر في وجه المراد
وتمنع القريحة عن الإذعان والإنقياد حتى خرجت الاوامر الشريفة المقدسة
النبوية المستظهرية بالإشارة إلى الخادم في تصنيف كتاب في الرد على
الباطنية مشتمل على الكشف عن بدعهم وضلالاتهم وفنون مكرهم واحتيالهم ووجه
استدراجهم عوام الخلق وجهالهم وإيضاح غوائلهم في تلبيسهم وخداعهم وانسلالهم
عن ربقة الإسلام وانسلاخهم وانخلاعهم وإبراز فضائحهم وقبائحهم بما يفضي الى
هتك أستارهم وكشف أغوارهم فكانت المفاتحة بالإستخدام في هذا المهم في
الظاهر نعمة اجابت قبل الدعاء ولبت قبل النداء وإن كانت في الحقيقة ضالة
كنت أنشدها وبغية كنت أقصدها فرأيت الامتثال حتما والمسارعة الى الإرتسام
حزما وكيف لا أسارع اليه وان لاحظت جانب الآمر ألفيته أمرا مبلغه رعيم
الأمة وشرف الدين ومنشؤه
ملاذ الأمم أمير المؤمنين وموجب طاعته خالق الخلق رب العاملين إذ قال
الله تعالى {أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول وأولي الأمر منكم}
وإن التفت إلى المأمور به فهو ذب عن الحق المبين ونضال دون حجة الدين
وقطع  لدابر الملحدين وإن رجعت إلى نفسي وقد شرفت بالخطاب به من بين سائر
العالمين رأيت المسارعة إلى الإذعان والامتثال في حقي من فروض الأعيان إذ
يقل على بسيط الأرض من يستقل في قواعد العقائد بإقامة الحجة والبرهان بحيث
يرقيها من حضيض الظن والحسبان الى يفاع القطع والاستيقان فانه الخطب الجسيم
والأمر العظيم الذي لا تستقل بأعيانه بضاعة الفقهاء ولا يضطلع بأركانه إلا
من تخصص بالمعضلة الزباء لما نجم في أصول الديانات من الأهواء
واختلط بمسالك الأوائل من الفلاسفة والحكماء فمن بواطن غيهم كان استمداد
هؤلاء فانهم بين مذاهب الثنوية والفلاسفة يترددون وحول حدود المنطق في
مجادلاتهم يدندنون ولقد طال تفتيشي عن شبه خصمه لما تقدر على قمعه وخصمه
وفي مثل ذلك أنشد ... عرفت الشر لا للشر ... لكن لتوقيه ... ومن لا يعرف
الشر ... من الناس يقع فيه ...
تظاهرت علي أسباب الإيجاب والإلزام واستقبلت الآتي بالاعتناق والإلتزام
وبادت الى الامتثال والارتسام وانتدبت لتصنيف هذا الكتاب مبنيا على عشرة
ابواب سائلا من الله سبحانه التوفيق لشاكله والصواب وسميته (فضائح الباطنية
وفضائل المستظهرية) والله تعالى الموفق لإتمام هذه النية وهذا ثبت الأبواب
الباب الأول في الإعراب عن المنهج الذي استنهجته في سياق هذا الكتاب
الباب الثاني في بيان ألقابهم والكشف عن السبب الباعث لهم على نصب هذه
الدعوة المضلة
الباب الثالث في بيان درجات حيلهم في التلبيس والكشف عن سبب الإغترار
بحيلهم مع ظهور فسادها
الباب الرابع في نقل مذهبهم جملة وتفصيلا
الباب الخامس في تأويلاتهم لظواهر القرآن واستدلالهم بالأمور العددية
وفيه فصلان الفصل الأول في تأويلهم للظواهر والفصل الثاني في استدلالالتهم
بالأعداد والحروف
الباب السادس في إيراد أدلتهم العقيلة على نصرة مذهبهم والكشف
عن تلبيساتهم التي زوقوها بزعمهم في معرض البرهان على إبطال النظر العقلي
الباب السابع في إبطال استدلالهم بالنص على نصب الامام المعصوم
الباب الثامن في مقتضى فتوى الشرع في حقهم من التكفير والتخطئة وسفك الدم
الباب التاسع في إقامة البرهان الفقهي الشرعي على أن الإمام الحق في
عصرنا هذا هو  الإمام المستظهر بالله حرس الله ظلاله
الباب العاشر في الوظائف الدينية التي بالمواظبة عليها يدوم استحقاق
الإمامة
هذه ترجمة الأبواب والمقترح على الرأي الشريف النبوي مطالعة الكتاب جملة
ثم تخصيص الباب التاسع والعاشر لمن يريد استقصاء ليعرف من الباب التاسع قدر
نعمة الله تعالى عليه وليستبين من الباب العاشر طريق القيام بشكر تلك
النعمة ويعلم ان الله تعالى إذا لم يرض أن يكون له على وجه الأرض عبد أرفع
رتبة من أمير المؤمنين فلا يرضى أمير المؤمنين ان يكون لله على وجه الأرض
عبد أعبد وأشكر منه نسأل الله تعالى أن يمده بتوفيقه ويسدده لسواء طريقه
هذه جملة الكتاب والله المستعان على سلوك جادة الحق واستنهاج مسلك الصدق
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-م-د (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is the opposite of blame (dhamm); it is to describe one with attributes of perfection while accompanied by love and veneration.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Qur'anic and theological register, ḥamd is the ascription of all perfection to God alone, grounded in His essential attributes, not merely in benefits received.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used here in its literal (ḥaqīqah) sense as genuine praise of God, not the metaphorical sense of mere thanks (shukr) for a specific favor.
- Root: ق-و-م (q-w-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To stand, to be upright, to undertake the management of a thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): al-Qayyūm is the One who sustains and manages all creation without needing anything Himself; His "standing" (qiyām) over all things is essential, not accidental.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal attribute of God; the "standing" of creatures is metaphorical (majāz) and contingent, whereas God's qiyām is real and necessary.
- Root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To succeed, to come after; also to differ, to be behind.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, ikhtilāf (difference) among the community is distinguished from tafarruq (schism); the former is a mercy when within the bounds of ijtihād, the latter a calamity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The author employs ikhtilāf here in its qualified sense — difference of opinion among the learned — as opposed to the condemned tafarruq of the Batinites.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of 'Aṭf (Coordination) with Reiterated Praise — The opening sequence of divine epithets (al-Ḥayy, al-Qayyūm, al-ʿAzīz, etc.) is a series of coordinated predicates (akhbār) of the implied subject "Allāh," each carrying independent theological weight, linked by the coordinating conjunction (wāw al-ʿaṭf) to build a cumulative doxological crescendo.
chapters.translation:
I say — and with God is the success:

[1] Praise be to God, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, upon whose essential subsistence no describer's description can prevail; the Majestic, whose attribute of glory no knower's knowledge can encompass; the Mighty, before whom no mighty one exists save that he stands bowed in humility at the threshold of His might; the Glorious, before whom no king exists save that he circles about the pavilion of His majesty; the Compeller, before whom no authority exists save that it hopes for the breaths of His pardon and fears the assaults of His wrath; the Proud, before whom no friend exists save that his heart is suspended upon love of Him and his body stands in service to Him; the Merciful, before whom nothing exists save that it rides upon the back of peril in the terror of the standing-places [of Judgment], were it not for His mercy reaching it through His prior and precedent promise; the Benefactor, who if He intends good for you, there is none to repel or avert His bounty; the Avenger, who if He touches you with harm, there is none to disclose it save Him. Glorified be His majesty and sanctified be His names — no ally deceives Him, no opponent harms Him. Exalted be His sovereignty — no schemer outwits Him, no open adversary contends with Him.

He created creation as factions and lineages, and ranked them in the embellishments of this world as the base and the noble. He drew them near in the realities of religion through connection and deviation, through ignorance and knowledge. He divided them in the foundations of creeds into groups and classes — they agree in harmony and separate in divergence. Thus they differed in their beliefs: in denial and acknowledgment, in waywardness and fairness, in moderation and excess, even as they differed in origin and attributes. One is rich, whose wealth multiplies daily, taking in abundance and spending in abundance. Another is weak, supporting weak offspring, lacking even a day's sustenance until he importunately begs of people. One is accepted in hearts, meeting in his need nothing but response and assistance. Another is hated by creation, his rights usurped through oppression and injustice. One is pious and divinely aided, increasing daily in his scrupulousness and godfearingness in abundance and radiance. Another is forsaken, increasing over the passage of days in his error and corruption in persistence and recklessness. That is the decree of your Lord, the Powerful, the Wise, from whose subjugation no authority can deviate; the Subduer, the Knowing, against whose judgment no one possesses opposition — in spite of the noses of the infidel Batinites, who denied that God makes difference among the people of truth, and did not know that difference among the community is followed by mercy, even as the lessons of their differences follow them in ranks and attributes.

And thanks be to God, who has granted us success in acknowledging His religion openly and secretly, and has guided us to submission to His judgment in manifestation and concealment, and has not made us among the misguided Batinites — those who display with their tongues acknowledgment but conceal in their breasts persistence and obstinacy; who carry burdens of sins while proclaiming in religion piety and gravity; who accumulate loads of wrongs, because they hope not for God's majesty. Were the callers of truth to address them night and day, their calling would only increase them in flight. When the sword of the people of truth looms over them, they prefer the truth with preference; and when its shadow withdraws from them, they persist and wax proud with arrogance. So we ask God that He leave not upon the face of the earth a single habitation of them. And we pray upon His chosen Messenger, and upon his family and his rightly-guided successors after him — prayers equal to the number of raindrops, pouring forth abundantly, increasing over the passage of days in continuity, and renewing over the succession of years in pursuit and repetition.

To proceed: I have not ceased, during my residence in the City of Peace (Baghdad), longing to serve the sacred, prophetic, imamic, Mustaẓhirian stations — may God multiply their majesty and extend their shadows over the strata of creation — by composing a book in the science of religion, through which I might discharge the thanks due for the blessing and establish the mark of service, and through which I might reap, by undertaking the burden, the fruits of acceptance and nearness. But I inclined toward delay, out of deliberation in determining the science I intended to treat and specifying the art that would find the place of satisfaction with the noble prophetic opinion. This perplexity continued to cast dust in the face of the intention and to prevent the faculty from yielding and submitting — until the noble, sacred, prophetic, Mustaẓhirian commands went forth, indicating to this servant that he compose a book in refutation of the Batinites, comprising the disclosure of their innovations and errors, the varieties of their deceit and stratagem, the manner of their seduction of the common folk and their ignorant masses, the clarification of their treacheries in their obfuscation and deception, their slipping from the noose of Islam, their sloughing off and divesting themselves [of it], and the exposure of their infamies and abominations — leading to the tearing of their veils and the uncovering of their depths.

The commissioning for this task was, in appearance, a blessing that answered before the supplication and responded before the call — though in reality it was a lost object I had been seeking and a desire I had been pursuing. So I saw compliance as an obligation and haste in submission as resolve. And how should I not hasten to it? If I consider the side of the commander, I find him a commander whose rank is the shepherd of the community and the honor of religion, whose origin is the refuge of nations — the Commander of the Faithful — and the obligation of obedience to him is from the Creator of creation, the Lord of the worlds, for God the Exalted has said: {«أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول وأولي الأمر منكم»} ("Obey God and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you"). And if I turn to the commanded matter, it is the defense of the manifest truth and the struggle on behalf of the proof of religion, and the cutting off of the trailing remnant of the heretics. And if I return to myself — having been honored with this address above all the worlds — I see that haste in yielding and complying is, in my case, among the individual obligations (furūḍ al-ʿayn), for rare upon the face of the earth is one who is competent in the foundations of creeds to establish the proof and demonstration, elevating them from the lowland of conjecture and supposition to the summit of certainty and conviction. For it is the grave matter and the great affair, whose burdens the merchandise of the jurists cannot bear, and whose pillars none can uphold save one specialized in the formidable difficulty — since there have arisen in the principles of religions the passions, and there have become intermingled with the paths of the ancients — the philosophers and the sages — and from the hidden depths of their error did these [Batinites] derive their sustenance. For they vacillate between the doctrines of the Dualists and the philosophers, and hover around the limits of logic in their disputations.

Long indeed was my search for the doubts of the opponent when I was unable to suppress him — and my opponent [was equally searching]. And in such a situation it is said:

"I came to know evil — not for evil's sake, but to guard against it; and he who knows not evil among people, falls into it."

The causes of obligation and compulsion converged upon me, and I faced what was coming with embrace and commitment, and hastened to compliance and submission. I set out to compose this book, built upon ten chapters, asking God the Exalted for success in its like and correctness. And I named it *The Infamies of the Batinites and the Virtues of the Mustaẓhirians* (فضائح الباطنية وفضائل المستظهرية). And God the Exalted is the granter of success for the completion of this intention.

This is the list of the chapters:

**Chapter One:** On the exposition of the method I have followed in the course of this book.

**Chapter Two:** On the explanation of their titles and the disclosure of the cause impelling them to erect this misguiding call.

**Chapter Three:** On the explanation of the degrees of their stratagems in obfuscation and the disclosure of the cause of being deceived by their stratagems despite the manifest corruption of them.

**Chapter Four:** On the transmission of their doctrine in summary and in detail.

**Chapter Five:** On their allegorical interpretations (ta'wīlāt) of the apparent meanings of the Qur'an and their inferences from numerical matters. It contains two sections: the first section on their interpretation of apparent meanings, and the second section on their inferences from numbers and letters.

**Chapter Six:** On the presentation of their rational arguments in support of their doctrine and the disclosure of their obfuscations which they have embellished — as they claim — in the guise of demonstration, for the invalidation of rational reflection (al-naẓar al-ʿaqlī).

**Chapter Seven:** On the invalidation of their inference from the [Qur'anic] text (naṣṣ) for the installation of the infallible Imam.

**Chapter Eight:** On what the legal opinion (fatwā) of the Law requires regarding them — of declaring them unbelievers, declaring them erroneous, and the shedding of their blood.

**Chapter Nine:** On the establishment of the juristic, legal proof that the true Imam in our present age is the Imam al-Mustaẓhir bi-llāh — may God guard his shadows.

**Chapter Ten:** On the religious functions by whose constant observance the entitlement to the Imamate endures.

This is the exposition of the chapters. And the proposal to the noble prophetic opinion is to review the book as a whole, then to single out the ninth and tenth chapters for whoever desires thoroughness — so that he may know from the ninth chapter the measure of God's blessing upon him, and may discern from the tenth chapter the way of undertaking the thanks for that blessing. And he will know that God the Exalted, when He is not pleased that there be upon the face of the earth a servant of higher rank than the Commander of the Faithful, so too the Commander of the Faithful is not pleased that there be for God upon the face of the earth a servant more worshipful and more thankful than himself. We ask God the Exalted to support him with His success and to guide him to the middle path of his way.

This is the sum of the book — and God is the one whose aid is sought for treading the high road of truth and pursuing the path of sincerity.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | الباب الأول في الإعراب عن المنهج الذي استنهجته في هذا الكتاب

لتعلم أن الكلام في التصانيف يختلف منهجه بالإضافة إلى المعنى غوصا
وتحقيقا وتساهلا وتزويقا وبالاضافة الى اللفظ إطنابا وإسهابا واختصارا
وايجازا وبالاضافة الى المقصد تكثيرا وتطويلا واقتصارا وتقليلا فهذه ثلاثة
مقامات ولكل واحد من الأقسام فائدة وآفة
وأما المقام الاول فالغرض في الغوص والتحقيق والتعمق في أسرار المعاني
الى اقصى الغايات التوقي من إزراء المحققين وقدح الغواصين فانهم إذا تأملوه
فلم يصادفوه على مطابقة أوضاع الجدال وموافقة حدود المنطق عند النظار
استركوا عمل المصنف واستغثوا كلامه واعتقدوا فيه التقاعد عن شأو التحقيق في
الكلام والإنخراط في سلك العوام ولكن له آفة وهي قلة جدواه وفائدته في حق
الأكثرين فإن الكلام إذا كان على ذوق المراء والجدال لا على مساق الخطاب
المقنع لم يستقل بدركه
إلا الغواصون ولم يتفطن لمغاصاته إلا المحققون وأما سلوك مسلك التساهل
والاقتصار على فن من الكلام يستحسن في المخاطبات ففائدته أن يستلذ وقعه في
الأسماع ولا تكل عن فهمه والتفطن لمقاصده أكثر الطباع ويحصل به الإقناع لكل
ذي حجى وفطنة وان لم يكن متبحرا في العلوم
وهذا الفن من جوالب المدح والإطراء ولكن من الظاهريين وآفته أنه من دواعي
القدح والإزراء ولكن من الغواصين فرأيت أن أسلك  المسلك المقتصد بين الطرفين
ولا أخلى الكتاب عن أمور برهانية يتفطن لها المحققون ولا عن كلمات إقناعية
يستفيد منها المتوهمون فان الحاجة الى هذا الكتاب عامة في حق الخواص
والعوام وشاملة جميع الطبقات من أهل الاسلام وهذا هو الأقرب إلى المنهج
القويم فلطالما قيل ... كلا طرفي قصد الأمور ذميم ...

### | المقام الثاني في التعبير عن المقاصد إطنابا وإيجازا وفائدة الإطناب الشرح والايضاح المغني عن عناء التفكر وطول التأمل وآفته الإملال وفائدة الايجاز جمع المقاصد وترصيفها وايصالها إلى الأفهام على التقارب وآفته الحاجة الى شدة التصفح والتأمل لاستخراج المعاني

الدقيقة من الألفاظ الوجيزة الرشيقة والرأى في هذا المقام الاقتصاد بين
طرفي التفريط والإفراط فإن الإطناب لا ينفك عن إملال والإيجاز
لا يخلو عن إخلال فالأولى الميل الى الاختصار فلرب كلام قل ودل وما أمل
المقام الثالث في التقليل والتكثير
ولقد طالعت الكتب المصنفة في هذا الفن فصادفتها مشحونة بفنين من الكلام
فن في تواريخ أخبارهم وأحوالهم من بدء امرهم الى ظهور ضلالهم وتسمية كل
واحد من دعاتهم في كل قطر من الاقطار وبيان وقائعهم فيما انقرض من الأعصار
فهذا فن أرى التشاغل به اشتغالا بالأسمار وذلك أليق بأصحاب التواريخ
والأخبار فأما علماء الشرع فليكن كلامهم محصورا في مهمات الدين وإقامة
البرهان على ما هو الحق المبين فلكل عمل رجال
والفن الثاني في إبطال تفصيل مذاهبهم من عقائد تلقوها من الثنوية
والفلاسفة وحروفها عن اوضاعها وغيروا ألفاظها قصدا للتغطية والتلبيس هذا
أيضا لا أرى التشاغل به لان الكلام عليها وكشف الغطاء عن بطلانها بايضاح
حقيقة الحق وبرهانها ليس يختص بالطائفة الذين هم نابتة الزمان فتجريد القصد
الى نقل خصائص مذاهبهم التي تفردوا باعتقادها عن سائر الفرق هو الواجب
المتعين فلا ينبغي أن يؤم المصنف في كتابه الا المقصد الذي يبغيه والنحو
الذي يرومه وينتحيه فمن حسن إسلام المرء ترك مالا يعنيه وذلك مما لا يعنيه
في هذا المقام وان كان
الخوض فيه على الجملة ذبا عن الاسلام ولكن لكل مقال مقام فلنقتصر في
كتابنا على القدر الذي يعرب عن خصائص مذهبهم وينبه على مدارج حيلهم ثم نكشف
عن بطلان شبههم بما لا يبقى للمستبصر ريب فيه فتنجلي عن وجه الحق كدورة
التمويه
ثم نختم الكتاب بما هو السر واللباب وهو إقامة البراهين الشرعية على صحة
الإمامة للمواقف القدسية النبوية المستظهرية بموجب الأدلة العقلية والفقهية
على ما أفصح عن مضمونه ترجمة الأبواب
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ه-ج (n-h-j)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A clear, open path or way; the beaten track that leads one to the goal.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The manifest method (manhaj) of proceeding in discourse, aligned with the straight path (ṣirāṭ) of truth.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for a physical road; metaphorical for a systematic course of reasoning or conduct.
- Root: غ-و-ص (gh-w-ṣ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To dive deep into water to extract something from the bottom.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Penetrating to the profound depths of meaning (maʿānī), as opposed to surface comprehension.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for pearl-diving; metaphorical for intellectual profundity in investigation (taḥqīq).
- Root: ق-ص-د (q-ṣ-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To aim, intend, or pursue a goal; the middle way (qasd) between extremes.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The intentional orientation of the soul toward an objective; also the equitable mean.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for aiming at a target; metaphorical for deliberate purpose and moderation in method.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqṣīr and Taʿlīq (Restriction and Suspension) — The author restricts the scope of discourse by conditional clauses and parenthetical qualifications, managing the reader's expectation across long periodic sentences.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the method of discourse in composed works varies in relation to meaning — whether by profundity, verification, leniency, or embellishment — and in relation to wording — whether by amplification, prolixity, abridgment, or concision — and in relation to purpose — whether by multiplication, prolongation, restriction, or reduction. These are three stations, and each of their divisions has both a benefit and a malady.

As for the first station, the aim in profundity, verification, and delving into the secrets of meanings to the utmost limits is to guard against the disparagement of the verifiers (muḥaqqiqūn) and the fault-finding of the deep divers (ghawwāṣūn). For when they examine a work and do not find it conforming to the canons of dialectic and the rules of logic as held by the speculative theologians, they disparage the author's labor, condemn his speech, and deem him to have fallen short of the summit of verification in discourse and to have slipped into the ranks of the common folk. Yet this station has a malady: its scant utility and benefit for the majority. For when speech is pitched to the taste of disputation and dialectic, not to the course of persuasive address, none comprehend it save the deep divers, and none perceive its diving-places save the verifiers.

As for pursuing the path of leniency and restricting oneself to a style of speech deemed commendable in ordinary address, its benefit is that its impact is relished by the ears, most temperaments do not weary of understanding it or perceiving its aims, and it secures persuasion for every possessor of intellect and sagacity, even if he is not deeply versed in the sciences. This style is among the things that attract praise and eulogy — but from the externalists (ẓāhiriyyūn). Its malady is that it invites fault-finding and disparagement — but from the deep divers.

So I resolved to pursue the moderate course between the two extremes, neither emptying this book of demonstrative matters that the verifiers may perceive, nor of persuasive expressions from which the less discerning may benefit. For the need for this book is general with respect to the elite and the commonalty alike, and encompasses all classes of the people of Islam. This is the nearest to the upright method. For it has long been said: "Both extremes of affairs are blameworthy."

As for the second station — expressing the aims with amplification and concision: The benefit of amplification (iṭnāb) is explanation and clarification that dispenses with the toil of reflection and prolonged meditation; its malady is tedium. The benefit of concision (ījāz) is gathering the aims, arranging them, and conveying them to the understandings in close succession; its malady is the need for intense scrutiny and meditation to extract the subtle meanings from the concise, elegant, and graceful words. My view in this station is economy between the two extremes of negligence and excess. For amplification is never free of tedium, and concision is never devoid of deficiency. The preferable course is to incline toward abridgment — for how often has little speech sufficed and indicated much, without causing weariness.

As for the third station — reduction and multiplication:

I have perused the works composed in this art and found them stuffed with two kinds of discourse. One kind concerns the histories of their reports and their conditions, from the beginning of their affair to the appearance of their error, naming each of their summoners (duʿāt) in every region, and relating their exploits in bygone ages. This is a kind of discourse that I deem occupying oneself with to be mere entertainment with tales; that is more fitting for the people of histories and reports. As for the scholars of the Sacred Law, let their speech be confined to the important matters of religion and the establishment of the proof concerning what is the manifest truth — for every work has its men.

The second kind concerns the refutation of the detailed doctrines they received from the Dualists (thanawiyya) and the philosophers, and how they displaced letters from their positions and altered their expressions, deliberately for the sake of concealment and obfuscation. This too I do not deem worthy of occupation, for discoursing upon them and unveiling their falsity by clarifying the reality of truth and its proof is not peculiar to the sect who are the upstarts of the age. Rather, directing the aim exclusively to transmitting the peculiarities of their doctrines — those in which they are unique among all other sects — is the obligatory and incumbent course. An author ought not to aim in his book at anything save the purpose he seeks and the path he intends and pursues. For part of a man's excellence in Islam is his leaving alone what does not concern him — and this does not concern him in this station, even though entering into it in general is a defense of Islam. But every speech has its station.

Let us therefore restrict ourselves in this book to what expresses the peculiarities of their doctrine and alerts to the stages of their ruses. Then we shall unveil the falsity of their doubts in a manner that leaves no room for doubt in the discerning one, so that the turbidity of obfuscation is cleared from the face of truth.

Then we shall conclude the book with that which is the secret and the kernel: the establishment of the legal proofs (barāhīn sharʿiyya) for the validity of the Imamate of the holy, prophetic, Mustaẓhirī stations, in accordance with the dictates of rational and juristic evidences — as the titles of the chapters declare their contents.
